articles.title: Após greve geral, Espanha aprova mudanças na habitação; medidas dependem da eleição no país | G1
articles.standfirst: Decretos aprovados ampliam a proteção contra despejos, limitam reajustes de aluguel e criam imposto sobre imóveis destinados a turistas; outras medidas ainda dependem de votação no Parlamento interino após as eleições, que acontecem em três semanas.
articles.summary: Decretos aprovados ampliam a proteção contra despejos, limitam reajustes de aluguel e criam imposto sobre imóveis destinados a turistas; outras medidas ainda dependem de votação no Parlamento interino após as eleições, que acontecem em três semanas.
articles.body:
Manifestantes entram em confronto com policiais durante uma greve geral nacional de 24 horas que reivindica salários suficientes para garantir acesso à moradia digna, em Barcelona, na Espanha. — Foto: Albert Gea / Reuters

A Câmara interina do parlamento espanhol ratificou nesta quinta-feira (12) medidas habitacionais destinadas a limitar despejos e especulação imobiliária.

A medida acontece no dia seguinte após a primeira greve geral em 14 anos no país . Manifestantes ocuparam as ruas das cidades espanholas contra a crise na habitação e no custo de vida.

A duração das medidas aprovadas, no entanto, provavelmente dependerá do resultado das eleições nacionais marcadas para o final deste mês.

O principal partido da oposição, o conservador Partido Popular, afirmou que revogará as medidas habitacionais do governo de esquerda caso chegue ao poder, o que, segundo as pesquisas, é uma possibilidade real.

“Ontem, o direito à moradia venceu nas ruas e nos locais de trabalho, e espero que vença novamente nas urnas”, disse a ministra interina da Habitação, Isabel Rodríguez, aos parlamentares.

O governo espanhol tentou aprovar as medidas em outubro, após a indignação pública com o aumento exorbitante dos aluguéis.

A crise aumentou após o despejo e subsequente morte de uma mulher de 87 anos em Madri , que foi televisionado em rede nacional.

Mas o PP e outros partidos conservadores se uniram no parlamento para rejeitar as medidas. Dias depois, o primeiro-ministro Pedro Sánchez convocou eleições antecipadas.

O governo então esperou para tentar novamente aprovar as medidas com um parlamento interino menor, em que ele e os partidos progressistas aliados tinham uma distribuição de assentos ligeiramente mais favorável.

O governo dividiu as medidas em dois decretos, sendo que uma delas, que desde o início parecia fadada ao fracasso, foi separada em um segundo decreto para não comprometer as demais.

O primeiro decreto, que continha um pacote de medidas, foi aprovado na quinta-feira, enquanto o segundo decreto foi, como esperado, rejeitado novamente.

A Câmara interina tem 69 membros, em comparação com os 350 do parlamento regular, que foi dissolvido quando as eleições foram convocadas.

O primeiro decreto foi aprovado por 35 votos a 34.

O decreto aprovado incluiu uma medida que estende a proteção contra despejos para inquilinos considerados pelos serviços sociais como estando em situação financeira ou social precária, desde que as autoridades regionais não possam oferecer-lhes uma residência alternativa.

Outra medida é a tentativa de reduzir a especulação imobiliária, impedindo que qualquer empresa envolvida no mercado imobiliário compre propriedades por menos de 70% do seu valor. A iniciativa visa coibir a compra em larga escala de imóveis a preços baixos e a subsequente revenda a preços mais altos.

O decreto também suspende os aumentos de aluguel para valores que já ultrapassam o preço de referência estabelecido pelo índice de preços do governo para aquele bairro em particular.

A lei estabelece ainda um imposto de 10% sobre apartamentos alugados para turistas — como aqueles em plataformas online como o Airbnb, que se tornaram alvo de críticas públicas — juntamente com um incentivo fiscal para estimular o arrendamento e empréstimos com garantia governamental para entrada em imóveis residenciais.

Parlamentares rejeitam novamente contratos de arrendamento por tempo indeterminado

O segundo decreto, que foi novamente rejeitado, previa a renovação automática dos contratos de arrendamento residencial pelos inquilinos. Caso os proprietários desejassem rescindir o contrato, teriam de indenizar os inquilinos com o valor correspondente a um ano de aluguel.

Muitos parlamentares consideraram que essa medida levaria os proprietários a retirarem seus imóveis do mercado de aluguel, provocando uma queda na oferta e preços ainda mais altos.

Ela foi rejeitada por 34 votos a 35, depois que um partido basco de centro-direita votou com o bloco de direita, após ter apoiado o outro decreto.

“Você nos prometeu mais moradias e só nos deu muita demagogia”, disse o deputado do PP, Sergio Sayas, ao ministro.

O PP prometeu supervisionar a construção de um milhão de novas casas, ao mesmo tempo que reduz drasticamente os impostos e a burocracia para o desenvolvimento imobiliário, caso retorne ao poder após oito anos de governo liderado pelos socialistas.

articles.title: Alertas de suposto 'apagão' em 17 de novembro: de onde veio boato  | G1
articles.standfirst: Teste de emergência nos EUA, série de alertas emitidos pela Defesa Civil de vários países e 'teoria' envolvendo 'Os Simpsons' impulsionaram boatos.
articles.summary: Teste de emergência nos EUA, série de alertas emitidos pela Defesa Civil de vários países e 'teoria' envolvendo 'Os Simpsons' impulsionaram boatos.
articles.body:
Alertas de suposto apagão mundial em 17 de novembro; veja perguntas e respostas — Foto: Reprodução

Nas últimas semanas, as redes sociais foram inundadas por uma "teoria" que prevê, sem provas ou evidências, um suposto "apagão global" de até três meses, a partir de 17 de novembro.

Para tentar dar credibilidade à previsão, os boatos nas redes misturam notícias e acontecimentos reais, mas que não têm qualquer relação comprovada entre si. Entre eles estão:

O agendamento de um teste do sistema de alerta de emergências dos Estados Unidos , marcado por agências federais americanas para o próximo dia 17.

Recomendações de agências governamentais do Reino Unido e do Brasil para estocar alimentos, água e outros itens essenciais para as primeiras 72 horas de uma emergência. Nos comunicados, as autoridades mencionam protocolos de prevenção para situações como desastres climáticos , mas não mencionam, em nenhum momento, um apagão global.

Recentes ataques hackers contra o sistema de refrigeração de supermercados na Europa e as redes do Porto de Santos .

Além disso, usuários nas redes também passaram a relacionar o suposto apagão a uma cena de "Os Simpsons" que mostra um blecaute na cidade fictícia de Springfield. O desenho é frequentemente associado, em memes e publicações nas redes, a supostas "profecias" sobre acontecimentos que teriam sido antecipados em seus episódios.

Mas a associação entre esses fatos não encontra respaldo técnico. Especialistas consultados pelo g1 explicam que um apagão simultâneo dessa proporção é tecnicamente extremamente improvável. Isso porque os sistemas elétricos dos países não funcionam como uma rede integrada, que poderia ser desligada de uma só vez.

Publicados no X, TikTok, Facebook e Instagram, os posts alcançam milhões de visualizações. Em um vídeo no Instagram com quase 3 milhões de views, um influenciador diz: "um apagão pode estar vindo, e 33 países já mandaram a população se preparar. Sem luz, sem Pix, sem cartão, sem internet".

Veja abaixo perguntas e respostas sobre o boato.

O que está programado para 17 de novembro?

A Agência Federal de Gerenciamento de Emergências dos EUA ( FEMA ), em coordenação com a Comissão Federal de Comunicações ( FCC ), realizará um teste nacional do Sistema de Alerta de Emergência (EAS) na terça-feira, 17 de novembro de 2026, por volta das 14h20, horário do leste dos EUA.

O anúncio foi feito em 30 de setembro no portal oficial das duas agências governamentais.

Em 17 de novembro de 2026, emissoras de rádio e televisão de todo o país interromperão a programação normal para transmitir uma mensagem de teste.

A mensagem de teste que chegará às televisões e aos rádios é a seguinte: “Este é um teste nacional do Sistema de Alerta de Emergência, emitido pela Agência Federal de Gestão de Emergências. Este é apenas um teste. Nenhuma ação é necessária por parte do público.”

A FEMA é obrigada por lei a realizar um teste nacional do sistema de alerta e aviso público pelo menos uma vez a cada três anos.

O Sistema de Alerta de Emergência é um sistema nacional de aviso público composto por milhares de provedores de rádio, televisão, cabo, satélite e banda larga fixa. Os testes permitem que a FEMA identifique eventuais problemas técnicos ou operacionais e verifique se o sistema está funcionando corretamente antes que ele precise ser acionado em uma emergência real.

E os pedidos de autoridades para estoque de itens essenciais?

Nas últimas semanas, autoridades governamentais de países da Europa e do Brasil divulgaram recomendações para que a população mantenha em casa alimentos, água e outros itens essenciais suficientes para garantir sua subsistência por até 72 horas em uma situação de emergência. As orientações têm caráter preventivo e não apontam para a previsão de nenhum evento catastrófico específico no futuro.

No Reino Unido, por exemplo, essa mensagem foi inserida na campanha "Be Ready" (Esteja preparado), que foi alvo de desinformação nas redes sociais. A iniciativa parte de um plano governamental de três anos de conscientização pública e foi lançada antes da temporada de inverno no país, período que tem sido marcado por uma série de tempestades severas.

No Brasil, em 8 de novembro, a Defesa Civil Nacional publicou instruções sobre como preparar um kit de emergência. "Em situações de grandes desastres, as equipes de socorro podem levar mais tempo para chegar. Por isso, é importante estar preparado para as primeiras 72 horas", disse parte da postagem.

O órgão deu orientação para o público reunir água potável, comida não perecível, utensílios e itens de primeiros socorros e de higiene, roupas, eletrônicos como rádio e lanternas, documentos pessoais e sacolas plásticas avulsas.

Os posts da Defesa Civil chamaram atenção e as pessoas reagiram nas redes. Parte dos usuários considerou o conteúdo um "exagero", enquanto outros associaram as recomendações à possibilidade de desastres climáticos. Também houve quem demonstrasse preocupação com a ideia de que "alguma coisa vai acontecer"

Diante da repercussão, o órgão fez uma nova publicação explicando que a recomendação não era um sinal de perigo.

"Falar de kit de emergência não é sinal de perigo, é sinal de que prevenir faz parte da rotina. A Defesa Civil Nacional posta diariamente conteúdos sobre prevenção. Por exemplo, conteúdos sobre "Kit de Emergência" foram postados dia 16 de março e 3 de abril".

O g1 também entrou em contato com o Ministério da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional ( MIDR ), responsável pela Defesa Civil, para perguntar por que a primeira postagem foi feita ao mesmo tempo em que países europeus davam orientações parecidas sobre kits de emergência.

Em resposta, o ministério afirmou que a Secretaria Nacional de Proteção e Defesa Civil (Sedec) divulga "regularmente" orientações de autoproteção para diferentes situações de emergência. "Entre essas orientações estão recomendações de como agir em diferentes situações de riscos e a organização de um kit doméstico de emergência".

A agência de notícias Reuters noticiou um ataque hacker que atingiu mais de 500 supermercados na França nas últimas semanas . As ações elevaram a temperatura dos refrigeradores para 50ºC durante a madrugada entre os dias 11 e 12 de outubro, causando incêndios e perdas de alimentos em centenas de lojas em todo o país.

No dia 2 de novembro, o mesmo ocorreu na Suécia, Irlanda, Holanda, Estônia, Finlândia, Bélgica e Luxemburgo, afetando os sistemas de refrigeração de mercados.

Sistemas financeiros também ficaram na mira dos ataques. Na França, o banco Crédit Mutuel Arkéa informou em 4 de novembro que foi alvo de um ataque hacker estimado em cerca de 100 milhões de euros (R$ 615 milhões). O ataque ocorreu menos de uma semana após a gigante das criptomoedas Binance ser alvo de uma ação semelhante.

Na semana passada, o alvo foi o setor aéreo. Vários voos comerciais receberam falsos alertas de ameaça de bomba a bordo, provocando transtornos em diferentes países.

Em declaração feita no dia 9 de novembro, o ministro das Relações Exteriores da França, Jean-Noël Barrot, acusou a Guarda Revolucionária do Irã de estar por trás dos ataques cibernéticos em uma campanha de "agressão híbrida" — mas sem fazer qualquer menção à possibilidade de um apagão na França ou na Europa. Por sua vez, o Irã nega ser responsável pelos ciberataques.

Um outro ataque hacker ocorreu nesta terça-feira (10) no Porto de Santos, em São Paulo.

A Autoridade Portuária de Santos (APS) confirmou que os sistemas ficaram indisponíveis após o ataque cibernético. O problema atingiu o site, os sistemas internos e os serviços utilizados por clientes e usuários do Porto de Santos. Apesar disso, a APS garantiu que não há risco de paralisação nas operações portuárias, embora possa haver lentidão e demora no atendimento administrativo. Um Gabinete de Crise foi criado para recuperar e coordenar medidas de resposta.

A Polícia Federal (PF) também instaurou um inquérito sobre o caso. A investigação aponta que o ataque veio de fora do país.

Os "Simpsons" previram um apagão mundial em 2026?

Uma mensagem viral nas redes sociais afirma que a série de desenho animado "Os Simpsons" previu no episódio " It's a Blunderful Life ", exibido em novembro de 2023, a ocorrência de um apagão global em 2026. A personagem Lisa relembra um apagão que deixou Springfield às escuras pouco antes do feriado no Dia de Ação de Graças. O episódio no entanto, não faz qualquer referência a um apagão mundial em 2026 e nem em 17 de novembro.

Em uma entrevista publicada em 2024 , o produtor executivo e showrunner da série, Matt Selman disse que as previsões dos Simpsons podem ser atribuídas a uma compreensão básica de duas disciplinas: história e matemática.

"Se você estuda matemática, sabe que, se a série faz literalmente milhares de piadas ao longo de quase 800 episódios, seria estatisticamente impossível não criar algum conteúdo que acabasse coincidindo com algo que aconteceria na vida real. Mas as pessoas preferem a resposta mais simples: “mágica”. Sinto que, na era atual de desinformação digital em que vivemos, as previsões dos Simpsons (ou, mais corretamente, “coincidências”) perderam o sentido. Qualquer pessoa, por mais desinformada que seja, pode gerar uma imagem com inteligência artificial baseada em algum evento atual e dizer: “Os Simpsons previram isso!” — e pessoas bem-intencionadas, mas facilmente enganadas, vão acreditar, simplesmente porque querem muito que isso seja verdade."

Por que o boato fala em 90 dias de apagão?

A menção aos 90 dias no boato tem origem no programa Fortress, do Departamento da Guerra dos Estados Unidos. O plano, no entanto, diz respeito à preparação de bases militares americanas para funcionar de forma independente, e não a um apagão que atingiria a população.

Segundo reportagem da "Fox News", intitulada "Por dentro do plano apocalíptico do Pentágono para manter os Estados Unidos em combate caso uma guerra global ecloda", publicada em 25 de outubro de 2026, o Pentágono está preparando instalações militares para manter operações essenciais por pelo menos 90 dias sem depender de estruturas externas. Isso inclui garantir o próprio acesso a eletricidade, água, combustível e sistemas de comunicação.

Ao g1 , Ildo Sauer , professor do Instituto de Energia Ambiental da Universidade de São Paulo ( USP ), explicou que a ocorrência de um ataque cibernético que desligasse toda a rede global simultaneamente é um evento de baixíssima probabilidade:

""Em primeiro lugar, nós temos uma diversidade de sistemas elétricos do planeta, nos países. O sistema do Brasil é um dos mais robustos em extensão no mundo. Os Estados Unidos têm cinco sistemas independentes. Na Europa, vários sistemas com certa autonomia, alguma interligação. A probabilidade de atacar isto simultaneamente é muito baixa. Isso demandaria um esforço muito grande de capacidade de atacar, adentrar, quebrar as senhas para colocar os ataques cibernéticos dos sistemas críticos. Fazer isso simultaneamente em todo o planeta é uma tarefa gigantesca".

Sauer complementa dizendo que os sistemas atuais possuem mecanismos de defesa para isolar áreas atacadas, preservando o resto da rede:

"Há as defesas internas e a resiliência de cada sistema que está programado para -- se houver um ataque a uma certa região, de certos subsistemas, uma usina geradora ou várias usinas, para retransmissão -- o sistema de distribuição desligar essas regiões atacadas e manter intacto o restante."

No relatório “Seamless Power Markets” (Mercados de Energia Integrados), publicado em 2014, a Agência Internacional de Energia (AIE) chega a uma conclusão semelhante à do docente da USP e afasta a hipótese de um grande apagão global com base em dois fatores principais:

Redes elétricas que funcionam de forma independente: O sistema elétrico mundial não funciona como uma única rede interligada. Ele é dividido em grandes sistemas que operam de forma independente, cada um com características próprias. Na Europa, por exemplo, a frequência da rede é de 50 Hz; na América do Norte, de 60 Hz. O relatório cita o caso da América do Norte, cuja rede é dividida em cinco grandes sistemas que não operam de forma sincronizada entre si: Western, Eastern, Texas, Alaska e Quebec. A troca de eletricidade entre essas redes depende de algumas linhas específicas, cuja capacidade é pequena em comparação com o volume total de energia consumido. Por isso, uma falha que provoque um apagão em um desses sistemas não se espalha automaticamente para os demais. Isso porque as quedas de energia desse tipo estão relacionadas a alterações na frequência elétrica dentro de uma mesma rede.

Governança e Operação Descentralizadas: “ A segurança do suprimento e o controle operacional permanecem sob jurisdição de governos locais e estaduais e de diferentes operadores de sistema (TSOs e ISOs/RTOs) com áreas de balanço independentes”.

articles.title: Produtor se emociona ao lamentar perda de 8 mil pés de uva após chuva | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva forte atingiu áreas rurais da cidade na manhã desta quinta-feira (12), também danificou uma lavoura de hortaliças e provocou quedas de árvores, segundo a Defesa Civil.
articles.summary: Além da perda de 8 mil pés de uva, a chuva de granizo em Indaiatuba destruiu hortaliças e derrubou árvores, gerando prejuízos de até R$ 250 mil para produtores rurais.
articles.body:
A chuva de granizo que atingiu Indaiatuba (SP) na manhã desta quinta-feira (12) destruiu parte de uma plantação de uvas no bairro Videiras, na região de Itaici. Ao todo, cerca de oito mil pés que estavam em uma área descoberta foram perdidos , segundo o produtor Valdomiro Cavalini..

O produtor mostrou à EPTV, afiliada da TV Globo, folhas e cachos de uva danificados pelo granizo. Ele contou que começou a registrar a chuva por volta das 6h , quando as pedras de gelo atingiram a propriedade. Emocionado, ele lamentou os estragos e falou sobre a incerteza diante do prejuízo.

"Complicadíssima. Nós aqui, realmente, oito mil pés, perdeu tudo. [...] Depois que passou a chuva, foi ver o prejuízo muito grande. [...] Só Deus na causa agora", relatou.

De acordo com Valdomiro, uma parte da plantação conseguiu ser preservada porque estava protegida por uma cobertura. Já a área descoberta ficou completamente comprometida. O produtor não informou o valor do prejuízo.

Os danos não ficaram restritos à produção de uvas. Outro produtor rural da região do bairro Videiras também teve uma lavoura de hortaliças atingida pela chuva . Segundo o proprietário, a intensidade da tempestade destruiu a plantação, e o prejuízo pode chegar a R$ 250 mil.

Moradores da região registraram a queda de granizo em vídeos enviados à EPTV. As imagens mostram a intensidade da chuva e os estragos provocados nas propriedades rurais.

Granizo atinge plantação e destrói 8 mil pés de uva em Indaiatuba — Foto: Reprodução / EPTV

De acordo com a Defesa Civil, ao menos 17 quedas de árvores foram registradas nesta manhã em Indaiatuba, principalmente nos bairros Itaici e Videiras, regiões com concentração de chácaras e propriedades rurais.

Outro ponto afetado foi a Estrada Municipal José Boldrini , que liga Indaiatuba a Itupeva (SP). A via está parcialmente interditada e funciona no sistema Pare e Siga. Um barracão foi destruído no local , e parte do telhado saiu do lugar.

Desde as primeiras horas do dia, equipes da Defesa Civil, da Guarda Civil e de secretarias municipais trabalham na remoção de árvores, limpeza e desobstrução das vias atingidas.

Ainda no bairro Videiras, a Escola Municipal Professor Eduardo Borsari ficou sem aulas no período da manhã devido à falta de energia elétrica. A CPFL informou que enviou equipes ao local para atender à ocorrência.

articles.title: Proclamação da República: veja o que abre e fecha em Fortaleza | G1
articles.standfirst: O Brasil celebra a data da Proclamação da República neste domingo (15). Confira como fica o funcionamento de órgãos públicos e estabelecimentos comerciais em Fortaleza.
articles.summary: Confira como fica o funcionamento de órgãos públicos e estabelecimentos comerciais em Fortaleza neste domingo (15)
articles.body:
O dia da Proclamação da República, celebrado neste domingo (15) em todo o Brasil, deve modificar o funcionamento de alguns serviços e comércios em Fortaleza .

Abaixo, confira o que abre e o que fecha em Fortaleza nesta data.

Confira o funcionamento dos principais shoppings de Fortaleza e Região Metropolitana no feriado deste domingo (15):

O Centro Fashion Fortaleza informou que ficará fechado neste domingo (15), como em todos os domingos e segundas-feiras do mês de novembro.

Cinépolis: programação disponível no aplicativo do shopping

Clínicas médicas: atendimento conforme horários agendados

Papai Noel: 15h às 21h (com intervalo das 17h às 17h30)

Cinema (UCI): funcionamento conforme horários das sessões

Praça de alimentação e lazer: 11h às 22h

Para facilitar o acesso dos alunos aos locais de prova do Enem 2026, as linhas de metrô e VLT em Fortaleza, Sobral e Cariri terão funcionamento gratuito neste domingo (15) .

O acesso será liberado pelas catracas, sem necessidade de apresentação de cartão de transporte, documentos ou comprovante de inscrição.

Pessoas não inscritas no Enem também poderão utilizar o serviço gratuitamente. O embarque de passageiros com bicicletas será permitido durante todo o horário de funcionamento.

➡️🚉 Confira os horários de operação neste domingo (15):

VLT de Sobral - Linha Sul: 10h33 às 18h48

VLT de Sobral - Linha Norte: 10h30 às 19h33

Por causa do funcionamento no domingo, que não costuma ter funcionamento do metrô e do VLT, as linhas vão encerrar mais cedo no sábado (14). É possível conferir os horários de funcionamento no site do Metrofor .

O Sindicato do Comércio Varejista de Derivados de Petróleo (Sindipostos-CE) informou que os postos de combustíveis em todo o estado funcionarão normalmente neste domingo (15).

As agências bancárias, que não funcionam aos domingos, também não estarão abertas neste dia 15 de novembro, de acordo com a Febraban (Federação Brasileira de Bancos).

Durante o feriado, as transações via PIX funcionam normalmente. Sites e aplicativos dos bancos também estarão disponíveis.

Contas de consumo, como água, energia e telefone, e carnês com vencimento no feriado podem ser pagos sem acréscimo no dia útil seguinte. Em geral, os tributos já são emitidos com datas ajustadas ao calendário de feriados nacionais, estaduais e municipais.

articles.summary: Huang era amante de Jensen Huang, que anunciou renúncia ao posto de CEO da Nvidia nesta quinta. Embora chinesa, ela vivia em Singapura e foi impedida de retornar por conta de uma investigação sobre possíveis infrações, segundo o governo local.
articles.body:
Alice Huang participando de um jantar organizado pelo CEO e cofundador da Nvidia. — Foto: AFP

Alice Huang, a suposta espiã chinesa envolvida no escândalo da fabricante de chips Nvidia após manter um caso com o ex-CEO da companhia, foi impedida de entrar de volta em Singapura, país onde vivia, anunciou o Ministério do Interior do país nesta quinta-feira (12).

O ministério afirmou ter barrado a entrada de Huang no país por conta de investigações em curso sobre possíveis infrações cometidas por ela.

➡️ De origem chinesa, Alice Huang está no centro do escândalo que culminou, também nesta quinta, com a renúncia de Jensen Huang, até então o poderoso CEO da Nvidia . O executivo — que, apesar do mesmo sobrenome, não tem parentesco com Alice — manteve um relacionamento extraconjugal com a mulher, que a Nvidia suspeita ser uma espiã chinesa que roubou informações da empresa . A Nvidia é dos Estados Unidos, que proíbe a transferência de tecnologia de chips de IA para a China.

Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed — uma empresa de Singapura cliente da Nvidia — havia deixado a Singapura em fevereiro. O ministério informou que ela foi investigada por possíveis irregularidades, incluindo a compra de servidores que foram exportados via Singapura para a Malásia, sem sequer ingressar no mercado singapuriano.

A ex-executiva foi investigada "por suspeita de envolvimento em possíveis infrações em Singapura, dada a sua posição, à época, como CEO, presidente do conselho e uma das principais controladoras da Megaspeed", declarou o ministério em um comunicado. O órgão ressaltou que a investigação não estava relacionada a espionagem.

Segundo o ministério, não houve provas suficientes para confirmar que Alice Huang tenha cometido qualquer infração; no entanto, ela forneceu à polícia "informações que sabia serem imprecisas" durante a investigação e minimizou seu papel na Megaspeed.

Ela recebeu uma advertência severa e foi proibida de retornar ao país, informou o ministério.

articles.standfirst: BNI Minas Partners foi lançado em 27 de outubro, no Espaço Arbóreo, e marca os cinco anos da organização na cidade, com mais de 25 mil referências de negócios trocadas.
articles.summary: BNI Minas Partners foi lançado em 27 de outubro, no Espaço Arbóreo, e marca os cinco anos da organização na cidade, com mais de 25 mil referências de negócios trocadas.
articles.body:
O BNI (Business Network International), maior organização de networking profissional do mundo, lançou no dia 27 de outubro sua quinta equipe em Juiz de Fora: o BNI Minas Partners. O evento marcou também os cinco anos de atuação da organização na cidade, onde a história começou em 2021, com a formação do BNI Minas Unique.

De lá para cá, a regional Zona da Mata e Vertentes já soma quase R$ 90 milhões em negócios fechados entre seus membros, todos gerados a partir de indicações. Nos últimos 12 meses, são mais de 25 mil referências (oportunidades de negócios) trocadas e 360 empresários participando em 11 equipes, cinco delas em Juiz de Fora.

Membros do BNI Minas Partners celebram o lançamento, no Espaço Arbóreo. — Foto: Cleverson Montanha

"O empresário de Juiz de Fora entendeu que networking não é trocar cartão. É construir relacionamentos de confiança que viram negócio. A quinta equipe é a prova de que esse movimento só cresce", afirma Rafael Fabri, diretor executivo do BNI Zona da Mata e Vertentes.

Rafael Fabri, diretor executivo do BNI Zona da Mata e Vertentes, durante o lançamento. — Foto: Cleverson Montanha

O modelo do BNI funciona de forma estruturada. Empresários de segmentos diferentes se reúnem semanalmente para gerar indicações qualificadas uns para os outros. Cada equipe tem apenas um representante por especialidade, o que elimina a concorrência interna e transforma cada membro em um promotor ativo do negócio do outro.

A filosofia que sustenta o método é o Givers Gain® (contribuir e ganhar na tradução literal): quem contribui para o crescimento do outro também recebe oportunidades por reciprocidade e gratidão. Presente em 77 países, o BNI trata o networking como estratégia de negócio, com metas, sistemas, acompanhamento e resultados mensuráveis.

O lançamento reuniu empresários de diversos segmentos no Espaço Arbóreo. A programação incluiu open networking, apresentação da metodologia do BNI e da nova equipe, palestras e um happy hour de relacionamento.

Empresários de diversos segmentos acompanham a programação do lançamento. — Foto: Cleverson Montanha

Um dos destaques foi a palestra de Rafael Rodrigues, empresário, fundador da Casa da Gráfica e da Donus Marketing e autor do livro A Era do Fundador.

Rafael Rodrigues, autor de A Era do Fundador, durante palestra no lançamento do BNI Minas Partners. — Foto: Cleverson Montanha

O BNI Minas Partners nasce para ampliar o acesso de empresários de Juiz de Fora a esse ambiente. A equipe tem como fundadora e diretora consultora Aline Rodrigues, especialista em gestão de pessoas e RH, tendo ainda várias especialidades disponíveis para novos membros.

"O Partners nasce de pessoas que acreditam que parceria é o caminho mais estratégico para crescer. Aqui reunimos empresários que querem gerar negócios de verdade e que estão dispostos a ajudar o outro a crescer também", diz Aline.

Empresários que querem conhecer a metodologia na prática podem visitar uma reunião de uma das cinco equipes do BNI em Juiz de Fora. O contato é feito pelo Instagram @bnizonadamataevertentes.

articles.title: Did China use a 'honeypot' to influence Nvidia CEO? US Congress wants answers
articles.summary: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang is facing growing pressure as US lawmakers raise concerns over whether his relationship with a woman suspected of having links to
articles.body: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang is facing growing pressure as US lawmakers raise concerns over whether his relationship with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence could have compromised American national security.On Wednesday, Congressman Jamie Raskin said Congress was more concerned about the possible impact of the alleged relationship on US national security than Huang's position as the head of the chipmaker."The fate of Mr Huang as the CEO of his companies is up to his board. Apparently, he exercises a lot of influence over his board," Raskin said, adding that the decision to retain or remove him was a matter for the company's directors.However, he said lawmakers had a legitimate reason to examine whether China had used an alleged "honeypot scheme" to influence a major American corporate executive.Raskin alleged that the woman, suspected of acting on behalf of China, may have influenced Huang, who in turn used his financial influence to persuade President Donald Trump to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced AI chips to China."Did this whole scheme end up compromising the national security of the United States? That is our legitimate interest," he said, adding that Congress was likely to hold oversight hearings on the matter.Earlier, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer criticised Trump for allegedly failing to act despite being briefed more than a year ago about Huang's reported relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.Schumer said the reports raised serious questions about the administration's handling of national security concerns involving one of America's most important technology companies."Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang, when he ought to be defending our national security," Schumer said.He also called on Congress to pass bipartisan legislation, including the AI Oversight Act, the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act, to restrict China's access to advanced American technology.Nvidia board weighs Jensen Huang's futureMeanwhile, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board of directors was preparing to remove Huang as CEO, citing people familiar with the matter. The reported move follows allegations about his relationship with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.Huang has acknowledged the alleged affair and reportedly discussed his infidelity with employees during meetings on Monday and Tuesday.Following his acknowledgement, Nvidia's board said it had launched an investigation into the matter. The probe is being led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.The New York Times separately reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.According to the NYT, Huang and Powell, 48, were captured on video behaving affectionately at a hotel in San Jose, California, during an Nvidia conference in March.Suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang in BeijingAdding to the row, Megaspeed International founder Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy at the centre of the scandal, is currently living in Beijing.Security officials are aware of her presence in the Chinese capital, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.A CBS News reporter also said in a post on X that Nvidia's board was preparing to discuss Jensen Huang's future, with the Trump administration aware of plans to remove him from the position.The controversy has also weighed on Nvidia's shares. CBS reported that the company's stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday following The Wall Street Journal's report, extending a multi-day decline.Nvidia was co-founded by Jensen Huang in 1993. The company designs some of the world's most powerful semiconductors, which are widely used by leading artificial intelligence firms. Its advanced chips are considered strategically important, with US export controls restricting their sale to China.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Drugs running was like 'paper round' for exploited son, mum says
articles.summary: More younger children are targeted by gangs as exploitation jumps by 85% in five years, BBC finds.
articles.body:
A mother whose son was groomed by a gang at the age of 13 before being taken into care claims the local authority housed him "right in the centre of exploitation", despite repeated pleas for help.

Within months of being recruited, she said her son was being forced to deliver drugs in Grimsby for up to 36 hours at a time – a "job" he got as easily as "a paper round".

The woman, who we are not identifying, said it took two years for North East Lincolnshire Council (NELC) to move her son to safety.

During that time, she said he was put at risk of continued exploitation because he was housed in accommodation she considered unsuitable.

He was eventually moved more than 250 miles (400km) away and his care placement cost £1.66m over two years.

NELC said it did not comment on individual cases, but took child criminal exploitation (CCE) extremely seriously and it was "a top priority" for the local authority and police.

"There are often very challenging situations and lessons are always being learnt," the council said.

Home Office data obtained by the BBC shows the woman, whom we are calling Sandra, is not alone in seeing her child being drawn into the world of criminality.

It shows the number of children recognised as victims of CCE in the UK almost doubled in five years to more than 3,000 in the last financial year.

One hundred and fifty three children identified as potentially at risk of criminal exploitation in North East Lincolnshire in 2025/26 – a rise of 56% in five years, with two thirds of cases aged 15 and under, according to NELC data.

At least two teenagers, including one facing prosecution, openly selling drugs including cocaine and ketamine on social media.

A 16-year-old boy, who is among a number of children at risk of exploitation, was charged with more than 30 crimes including assault, burglary, theft and drug offences. He continued to offend after being sentenced.

A former NELC care worker said she was seeing an increasing number of younger children being exploited, with some "offered a bag of chips to go and get drugs".

Sandra contacted the BBC in response to a report about teenagers boasting on TikTok about stealing motorbikes .

Sandra said her son, who has autism and ADHD, was first groomed by a criminal gang at the age of 13.

Within months, he became involved in substance misuse, was frequently disappearing from home and had been recruited to steal motorbikes and deliver drugs.

"My son had been going missing," said Sandra, who works in the legal profession.

"There was no normality to what we were going through. [He] was so chaotic. We were frightened for our lives.

"I knew deep down this was not teenage behaviour. It was extreme.

"Within months, between Easter and the start of the new school term, that was it. I'd lost my son."

Sandra said she repeatedly asked the local authority for help as his behaviour rapidly deteriorated, with family members fearing for their safety.

"He was thin and gaunt. He looked ill and was covered in scars, bruises and injuries," she said.

At the age of 14, Sandra's son was taken into care following what she described as a breakdown linked to addiction and exploitation, which she said left the family unsafe due to his violent behaviour.

However, Sandra said she believed professionals failed to recognise the scale of exploitation in Grimsby when he was "placed right in the centre of the exploitation" in the town.

"I believed professionals understood these risks in the community around exploitation and I leaned on them to help give me some answers and to enable me to continue to be a mum. But the absolute opposite happened."

He was later moved to another care home 250 miles (400km) away, but within weeks the teenager fled and returned to Grimsby, before he was sent back.

In that time, the teenager was charged with a number of offences, including assault, which he committed before he was removed from the area. Following guilty pleas at Grimsby Magistrates' Youth Court in October, he received a conditional discharge, meaning he will be punished if he reoffends within the next two years.

Sandra said she had not given up hope in bringing her son home, adding: "I won't stop until we get him back."

Data obtained by the BBC through a freedom of information (FOI) request showed NELC spent almost £9m on out-of-area placements for 28 exploited children who were in care between 2021/22 and 2025/26.

The BBC identified at least three cases in which youngsters later fled care homes and returned to Grimsby, with two going on to commit offences.

The same NELC figures show the risk of criminal exploitation is increasingly affecting younger children, with the number of cases involving those aged nine and under, who are potentially vulnerable, more than doubling from 12 to 25 in the last financial year.

Of the 153 children identified as being at risk of potential exploitation in 2025/26, 108 were aged between 13 and 17 – the highest level for five years.

The council said it had seen an increase in children being identified as potentially vulnerable to exploitation because of improved information sharing and earlier intervention.

However, the Home Office statistics reveals a starker national picture, with an 85% increase in the number of CCE victims between 2021/22 and 2025/26.

One former NELC care worker, who wishes to remain anonymous, told the BBC: "I know of children as young as eight and nine who have been offered a bag of chips to go and get drugs.

"I've seen children having to deal drugs from children's homes because we can't keep them safe anymore. They're too scared to not deal the drugs."

Jane, not her real name, claimed workforce shortages, high staff turnover and reliance on agency workers were affecting safeguarding and putting children at risk of being deliberately targeted by criminal gangs.

New figures obtained by the BBC through a separate FOI request show a 20-fold increase in the number of agency workers used by NELC in its children's homes, from four in 2021/22 to 81 in 2025/26.

Between March 2022 and September 2026, almost £1.4m was spent by the council on agency supply staff.

The data also shows a relatively high turnover of staff in some care homes. In one, 18 left during the last financial year, compared with three in the previous 12 months.

"I think our social care system is breaking at the moment," said Jane. "We're losing staff at a pace of knots."

She claimed agency workers often lacked adequate training and detailed knowledge of individual children, making it harder to identify patterns of risk and protect them.

"We're not forwarding information as we should to the police, which is then leaving the children more vulnerable," she added.

Evidence seen by the BBC shows concerns were repeatedly raised with the council over a number of years about exploited children being left in unsafe situations and staff being ignored when they flagged serious incidents.

Children's commissioner Dame Rachel de Souza described how the "sheer scale of this abuse is deeply concerning".

She said it was "wholly unacceptable" that children taken into care could still find themselves in environments "where they remain exposed to the very dangers they should be protected from".

NELC said it was "confident that we have the right approach, putting the safeguarding of our young people at the core of what we do".

The authority said its continued priority "is to protect children, support families, disrupt exploitation" and it was taking "a proactive, preventative approach".

The BBC spent three days in youth courts in September and October, where cases involving a dozen children from North East Lincolnshire, including one as young as 12, were heard. Charges included assault, theft, burglary, drugs offences, criminal damage and dangerous driving.

By cross-referencing the names of those children with other sources, the BBC learnt about half of those children were at risk of CCE. Among them was a 16-year-old boy given a 12-month youth rehabilitation order at Grimsby Magistrates' Court after he pleaded guilty to carrying out more than 30 offences over a two-year period, including burglary and drugs possession.

During his sentencing, magistrates heard how there was a shortage of residential placements for children in care.

The BBC understands the boy had been placed more than 100 miles (160km) away, but returned to the town committing some of the offences he admitted.

Court documents show he has continued to offend despite being sentenced.

Ch Supt Craig Nicholson, head of safeguarding at Humberside Police, said CCE was "a complex crime to investigate".

"It is important to acknowledge that not every child who commits an offence is being criminally exploited, but every child involved in crime should be considered in the context of their age, circumstances, vulnerability and the potential influence of others," he added.

Policing minister Sarah Jones said a new child criminal exploitation offence would be introduced, targeting gangs who draw children into crime.

Five years ago, Ofsted rated the NELC's children's services inadequate when it found children were being exposed to harm because of "widespread weaknesses" in the department.

A government commissioner was subsequently appointed and a new management team brought in.

An Ofsted report last year stated services had improved and were rated good overall, with leadership and support for care leavers judged outstanding.

articles.title: Happy Children’s Day 2026: Easy speech ideas for students and teachers to inspire young minds on 14 November
articles.summary: Children's Day, also called Bal Diwas, is celebrated across India every year on November 14.
articles.body: Children's Day, also called Bal Diwas, is celebrated across India every year on November 14. It is a day for children when schools hold programmes, songs, plays and speeches. The day reminds the country that children's care, education and happiness matter.It marks the birthday of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, who was born on 14 November 1889 in Allahabad, adored children and spoke up for their rights to education, making knowledge accessible to all. Children fondly called him "Chacha Nehru."Interestingly, India did not always celebrate on this date. Before Nehru's death, Bal Diwas was held on 20 November, the day the United Nations marks as Universal Children's Day. After he died on 27 May 1964, the Indian Parliament passed a resolution making his birthday, 14 November, the official Children's Day. So the date was chosen to honour his love for children, who was so close to them.Every year, many students and teachers stand on a school stage to give a speech for this day. But the night before Children’s Day is filled with turmoil about how to make that speech more than a list of greetings. To solve this problem, here are some speech ideas for Children’s Day 2026.A good Children's Day speech is more than a set of quotes or greetings. It should inspire, remind children how special they are, and help them dream bigger. The right words, it says, can stay with children long after the celebration ends.Start with why the day existsTry opening your speech with the true meaning of the day. Children's Day is not only about sweets and celebrations, but about seeing children as the foundation of the nation. It brings in Chacha Nehru's belief that "children are like buds in a garden," which need care, guidance, and chances to bloom. His love for children was about giving them education, equality, and a voice, not just affection, which is also why it makes the day so special.Deliberate your speech by including a storylineRather than quoting famous people, try to tell a simple story that touches the heart. It could be about a child who helped a friend, stood up for what's right, or turned a small kindness into something big. One example is a student who helped another child learn to read, showing that leadership can begin early.Talk about dreams and valuesA speech works best when it encourages children to dream freely. It should remind them that education is about curiosity, empathy, and courage as much as marks. Try telling children to believe in their ideas, ask questions, and keep learning, and use the line: "Every great discovery once began with a question asked by someone your age."Cite examples of real life role modelsTry going beyond just historical figures and talk about young inventors, student activists or artists who made a difference before turning 18. When children hear about others like them, they start to see what is possible for themselves.Thank parents and teachersA thoughtful speech also salutes the adults who raise children. To make the speech innovative, try to include a short note to thank and recognise parents and mentors, which can remind everyone that a supportive environment is the best gift a child can get. Listening and encouragement matter more than perfection, and when adults make room for children's voices, they help build confident, kind, and creative citizens.Try concluding the speech with a ray of hopeFor the conclusion of the speech, the article chooses a message that tells us to stay kind, curious, and brave in a world that often asks children to grow up too fast. Try ending with the line, "Every smile, every question, and every dream adds light to the world, so make sure you continue being curious!"Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Roberto Clemente's three sons sought $45 million after Puerto Rico put the baseball legend's image on commemorative plates; the US Supreme Court refused their appeal on November 9, leaving other claims unresolved
articles.summary: A sporting legend's legacy can live far beyond the stadium, but deciding who controls that legacy can become a complicated legal battle.
articles.body: A sporting legend's legacy can live far beyond the stadium, but deciding who controls that legacy can become a complicated legal battle. More than half a century after Roberto Clemente's death, his name and image have become the subject of a dispute between his family and his native Puerto Rico. In 2022, the US territory issued souvenir license plates featuring the baseball star without his sons' consent, causing a dispute. Now, the US Supreme Court's refusal to hear their appeal has left the family's fight over trademark rights and compensation unresolved.Supreme Court declines to interveneAccording to Reuters and ESPN, the Supreme Court declined on November 9 to consider an appeal filed by Clemente's three sons against Puerto Rico's use of their father's likeness on commemorative licence plates and vehicle registration tags.Roberto Clemente Jr, Luis Roberto Clemente and Roberto Enrique Clemente had challenged the programme, arguing that the government had appropriated trademark rights belonging to the family. Their lawsuit, filed alongside two companies they own that work to protect Clemente's brand and philanthropic legacy, sought to prevent future use of his image on vehicle plates.The family also sought $45 million in damages and an additional $3.15 million in compensation for trademark infringement. The sons maintained that the programme generated approximately $15 million for Puerto Rico through the sale of the commemorative registrations.The Supreme Court rejected the appeal without providing an explanation. However, the decision does not resolve every aspect of the wider dispute. According to Reuters, the family's legal representatives intend to continue pursuing the claims that remain before the lower courts.How the commemorative plates sparked a disputePuerto Rico introduced the special plates and registration tags in 2022 to mark the 50th anniversary of Clemente's death. The designs featured his portrait, his iconic Pittsburgh Pirates jersey number 21 and recognition of his remarkable achievement of recording 3,000 career hits.According to USA Today, the registration programme involved fees of $21 and $5, which collectively generated around $15 million for the territory. The initiative was introduced during a difficult economic period, as Puerto Rico continued recovering from bankruptcy.Clemente's children objected to the arrangement because the revenue went to the government rather than businesses associated with preserving and promoting their father's legacy. The programme was discontinued at the end of 2022.The family subsequently filed a lawsuit, arguing that the unauthorised commercial use of Clemente's identity amounted to a government taking of private property under the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution.Trademark rights at the centre of the legal battleThe central question concerned whether constitutional protections against government seizure of private property extend automatically to intangible assets such as trademarks.A federal district court in San Juan, presided over by Judge Gina Méndez-Miró, dismissed the family's case. The Boston-based 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals subsequently upheld parts of that decision, rejecting the argument that Puerto Rico's use of the trademarks constituted an unconstitutional taking.According to Reuters and ESPN, the family's lawyers argued before the Supreme Court that the lower courts had weakened constitutional safeguards by treating trademark rights differently from physical property.Puerto Rico claimed the appeals court can protect intangible property under the Constitution. Its legal representatives argued that the decision simply applied existing Supreme Court precedents to the circumstances of the case.Remembering a baseball iconThe dispute concerns the legacy of one of baseball's most celebrated players. Born in Carolina, Puerto Rico, Clemente spent 18 seasons with the Pittsburgh Pirates between 1955 and 1972.He earned 15 All-Star selections, won two World Series championships and finished his career with exactly 3,000 hits, alongside a .317 batting average, according to USA Today. He was inducted posthumously into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1973.Clemente died on December 31, 1972, aged 38, when the aircraft carrying him humanitarian supplies to earthquake victims in Nicaragua crashed.His sporting achievements and humanitarian contributions have made his identity an enduring part of baseball history. His sons' remaining legal claims mean the dispute over who controls and profits from Clemente's image may continue after the Supreme Court's Nov. 9 decision.Images Courtesy: istock and Roberto Clemente websiteYou use AI every day. articles.title: This winter, it’s polar vortex versus El Niño. Round one starts now
articles.summary: This winter is shaping up to be very unusual as a record-early polar vortex disruption meets a historically strong El Niño.
articles.body: High in the atmosphere above the Arctic, something strange is happening: the polar vortex has broken down earlier than ever recorded, a phenomenon that can trigger a blast of cold weather in parts of the Northern Hemisphere. However, there’s also another unprecedented force at work in the form of a historically strong El Niño, which typically drives warmer global temperatures. It’s setting up an atmospheric battle for influence over our weather — and it’s not yet clear which will win. ❄️ See when the coldest air arrives for you in the CNN Weather app The polar vortex is a belt of strong winds high in the atmosphere that tightly hugs the Arctic’s frigid air, keeping it locked up around the North Pole. It forms every fall as the sun sets on the top of the world and the dark Arctic nights begin. Although it exists in the stratosphere, about 10 to 30 miles above the Earth’s surface, it can play a strong role in shaping the Northern Hemisphere’s winter weather patterns. For the past few weeks, the polar vortex has been weakening. Right now, the air in the stratosphere is warming dramatically in a phenomenon known as a “major sudden stratospheric warming” event, where the polar vortex’s winds reverse. In the days and weeks after this happens, Arctic air can spill south into the Northern Hemisphere, loading the dice in favor of cold air outbreaks. “This year is exceptionally unique,” said Andrea Lopez Lang, a meteorologist at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Major stratospheric warming events typically occur between January and March, with the previous earliest event happening on November 28 in both 1968 and 2025. It’s not yet clear why this disruption is happening so early. It’s possible El Niño may have played a role — some research has linked it to a weaker polar vortex and more frequent major disruptions. “But we’re not sure yet,” said Simon Lee, an atmospheric scientist at the University of St Andrews. What’s certain is that its unprecedented nature makes it hard to understand exactly how the impacts will play out and where. “It’s happening so early in the season that basically our historic events don’t capture what’s actually happening,” Lopez Lang said. The first taste of winter Parts of the US and Europe will get their first taste of winter this week, with a blitz of cold conditions that may have ties to the polar vortex disruption. A blast of Arctic air spilled out over North America and Europe Wednesday, which will last into the weekend — with peak cold on Thursday or Friday for most places. This will mean widespread frost, the first for much of the Eastern US and Northwest Europe. This cold is not expected to be particularly extreme but will be a sharp break from the unusual warmth of summer and fall in places such as the US East Coast and the UK. In the US, nearly everywhere east of the Mississippi River will experience the coldest weather since spring, with most of the eastern half of the country enduring temperatures around 7 to 14 degrees Fahrenheit below mid-November averages. Similar anomalous cold will also affect northern Europe. This cold snap will not linger long, however, with above average temperatures set to return in the eastern US and other regions next week. This week may just be the “appetizer,” with the more impactful “main course” still to come, said Judah Cohen, an MIT climatologist. The effects of a disruption typically take a few weeks to filter down, and there’s an increased risk of colder weather to both eastern North America and northern Europe in late November or early December, he said. The El Niño factor Polar vortex disruptions don’t automatically translate to blockbuster cold, especially when they happen earlier in the season before the Arctic cold has had a chance to really build — and when there’s a super-sized El Niño to contend with. El Niño is the “big bully pushing the atmosphere in a certain direction,” Lopez Lang said. She thinks its impact will be “so overwhelming” that while we may see some cold air, it’s unlikely to be anything outside of what would be expected during a typical winter season. Amy Butler, a research physicist at NOAA’s Chemical Sciences Laboratory, echoes this. “The feature that stands out to me over the next month, is the higher chance of warm temperatures over the northern half of the US, likely related to El Niño,” she said. Some disagree. There’s an assumption that “El Niño is kind of this runaway freight train, and nothing’s going to get in the way of it,” MIT’s Cohen said. It is important, he added, but “whether there’s cold air or not will depend on the behavior of the polar vortex.” There’s the impact of global warming to consider, too, said Jason Furtado, an associate professor of meteorology at the University of Oklahoma. Winters are warmer on average than they were just a few decades ago. “That means everything is relative when we talk about any potential cold air outbreak,” he said. An atmospheric experiment It looks like the polar vortex will strengthen again quickly after this event, said NOAA’s Butler. “It might be that this disruption doesn’t have much staying power,” she said. But there may be further polar vortex disruptions to come. “I wouldn’t be surprised if we saw another one this winter,” Lopez Lang said. “And the next one might be the one that we actually have the impacts from.” This unique winter will give scientists the chance to see whether El Niño is taking charge of the weather or whether the polar vortex can still flex its considerable muscle. “The atmosphere is setting itself up to be an experiment,” said Lopez Lang. “I think is going to be really exciting to see.” CNN’s Andrew Freedman contributed reporting.

articles.title: Garth Brooks: Country legend adds extra Belfast 2027 gig
articles.summary: Brooks will play three outdoor concerts at Boucher Road Playing Fields on 21 and 22 May 2027.
articles.body:
American country music star Garth Brooks has added an extra Belfast date to his 2027 tour after his two original shows in the city sold out.

The new date, an outdoor concert at Boucher Playing Fields, will take place on 23 May.

Brooks will also play two gigs at the same location on 21 and 22 May 2027. The gigs will be the first time he has performed in Belfast since 1998.

Brooks' last gigs in the city were a five-night run at the King's Hall in November 1998, after which he said the reaction from fans left his ears "ringing for three days".

Next year's concerts in Belfast will be the first of 11 on the island of Ireland, with two shows each in Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick and Cork.

Brooks announced the extra Belfast date in a social media post on Thursday.

Peter Aiken, from Aiken Promotions, told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that the new Belfast gig is "red hot".

"There could be a fourth show in Belfast," Aiken said.

Some of the Oklahoma singer's biggest hits include Friends in Low Places, If Tomorrow Never Comes and Callin' Baton Rouge.

Brooks is the biggest selling artist in US history as the only artist to pass 200 million albums sold.

Brooks last performed in Ireland in September 2022.

More than 400,000 tickets were sold for five concerts at Dublin's Croke Park.

articles.title: Young voters are not buying socialism. They want a made-in-America future
articles.summary: The Republican Party faces a young voter crisis as 73% backed Democrats in midterms, driven by housing costs and doubts about the American Dream.
articles.body: Young voters sent warning after warning to a Republican Party that remained tone-deaf, and one came wrapped in foil. When a Turning Point USA student complained that a burrito should not cost $20, some conservatives shifted the blame by lecturing young Americans to cook at home, eat ramen, find roommates and work additional jobs. "Burrito-gate" produced plenty of online jokes, but the frustration was never merely about lunch. It was about whether hard work still produces a better life. President Trump brought voters under 30 close to an even split in 2024 and won a majority of young men, proving that this generation was willing to move right. However, the midterm election proved they were just as willing to move left toward the party they believed offered a more affordable future. A Fox News Voter Poll found that voters under 30 supported Democratic House candidates by 73% to 25%. Young voters shifted left even as the broader electorate continued to favor capitalism over socialism. The same national poll found that 57% viewed capitalism favorably, while only 33% viewed socialism favorably. However, 69% believed the economy favors the wealthy. This shows the Republican hurdle: Americans believe in capitalism but doubt that today’s economy allows everyone to participate in the American Dream. A recent Harvard Youth Poll found that only 20% of young Americans said the democratic socialist label would make them more likely to support a candidate, while 31% said it would make them less likely and 45% said the label made no difference. Economic frustration gave Democrats an opening, but it did not turn an entire generation into blanket socialists. BURRITO DEBATE RIPS OPEN GOP CIVIL WAR ON AFFORDABILITY: ‘WE WILL LOSE, AND DESERVE IT’ The Republican Party of family, faith and freedom tells young men to "man up," work hard, marry, become fathers and provide for their families. Young women are expected to "do it all" by working, building careers, marrying and becoming mothers. Building a Made-in-America life requires all young adults to afford bills, groceries and rent instead of living paycheck to paycheck. If they cannot afford housing of their own, guess where they are living? They are living with parents who are absorbing the affordability gap. The Federal Reserve found that 47% of adults ages 18–29 received outside help paying an expense, while 49% of adults under 30 lived with a parent, up 12 percentage points since 2019. Republicans cannot tell young men to man up or promise young women a future of homeownership, marriage and children while their parents are forced to finance the gap between a paycheck and independence. I'M GEN Z: IF THE GOP WANTS MY VOTE, STOP THE SPEECHES AND FIX THE HOUSING CRISIS Republicans must answer this frustration with a competence revolution that builds more attainable housing, removes barriers to ownership and turns a paycheck into independence. The strongest defense of capitalism is to build a nation of owners. Right now, young voters experience the economy through rent, debt and bills, not through ownership of their first home. Republicans should measure success results that families can see: faster permit approvals, more starter homes and rent or mortgage. The revolution begins with housing. Currently, local fees, slow permitting, outdated zoning and land-use restrictions and barriers to manufactured housing limit supply and increase construction costs. Every Democratic proposal should face a litmus test: Does it produce more homes or just more government handouts to compete over the same limited supply? Scarcity only benefits investors by keeping more Americans renting longer, while existing homeowners gain equity as restricted supply drives property values higher. Local governments collect development fees, and large developers easily absorb delays that drive smaller builders out. Ultimately, every added fee and delay lands on the bill of first-time homebuyers. TRUMP ACCOUNTS ARE JUST THE BEGINNING. YOUNG AMERICANS NEED A PATH TO HOMEOWNERSHIP President Trump provided a blueprint for restoring the American Dream of homeownership through executive order by directing federal agencies to reduce regulatory barriers and create best practices for states and localities, including caps on permitting timelines and fees. He expanded that affordability agenda by directing the creation of a pilot program to proactively cancel mortgage-insurance premiums after qualifying homeowners build sufficient equity, lower refinancing costs and promote lower-cost factory-built housing. Republicans must accelerate these reforms and require officials receiving federal housing dollars to report permit times, construction fees and the number of homes produced in real time. The American Dream should be measured by homes built, costs reduced and more first-time buyers becoming homeowners. Republicans can tell young men to man up and young women to do it all, but they must build an economy in which stepping up still leads to a home, a family and a future. That is how Republicans defeat socialism: Make the American Dream affordable again.

articles.title: China says US ‘fabricating’ Nvidia spy claims to justify tech ‘blockade’
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO is under investigation for an affair with a woman whom US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.
articles.body:
China has urged ⁠⁠⁠⁠the ⁠⁠⁠⁠United States to stop “fabricating so-called spy narratives and ⁠⁠⁠⁠using them as a pretext for imposing ⁠⁠⁠⁠a technological blockade”, amid national security concerns that emerged over an affair involving Nvidia’s CEO.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the comments at a press briefing on Thursday when asked about allegations that the woman with whom Nvidia’s Jensen Huang had a relationship was a Chinese spy.

Mao said that China’s scientific and ⁠⁠⁠⁠technological progress was ⁠⁠⁠⁠driven by independent innovation and open cooperation, adding that Beijing was willing ⁠⁠⁠⁠to work with the US to implement a consensus reached ‌‌‌‌by their two heads of state. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to ease tariffs and lift restrictions on tech to de-escalate tensions following tit-for-tat tariffs in a trade deal in Busan , South Korea.

The remarks come ahead of a meeting next week between Trump and Xi at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen, southern China.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into the world’s leading supplier of the chips that power artificial intelligence (AI), has admitted to having an extramarital affair. The woman was reported to be Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence.

Megaspeed on Thursday said it takes compliance obligations under US export control laws “extremely seriously” and that it “is committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government”.

Nvidia’s 63-year-old boss has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced chips to China. Last year Trump cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export to China despite objections from Republicans and Democrats who fear Chinese dominance in AI technology.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied the claims, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

Huang’s position at the top of the $4.2 trillion company hangs in the balance after Nvidia launched an investigation into him on Sunday. It is unclear whether the tech giant has a succession plan.

articles.title: NYC building collapse: Eight bodies recovered as first responders search for survivors
articles.summary: FDNY crews are continuing rescue operations in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighborhood after a three-story building collapsed Wednesday, leaving at least 8 dead.
articles.body: Eight bodies have been recovered from the rubble of a three-story building that collapsed in New York City on Wednesday afternoon, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. The FDNY initially reported two fatalities after the building collapsed in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighborhood, but the death toll has continued to rise as rescue crews find more bodies. "This has been a devastating evening and morning for our city. Eight of our fellow New Yorkers, six adults and two children, have died as a result of a three story building collapse here at 1321 Flatbush Avenue. Six of those New Yorkers passed away on the scene. Two others died at nearby hospitals," Mamdani said. "As of now, we have confirmed the two of those who died were construction workers at 2625 Bedford Avenue. Eighteen other people were injured from the collapse, 14 civilians and four firefighters," he added. "The vast majority of those still being treated in hospitals are in stable condition. One person is in critical condition." The rescue operation is ongoing with over 250 fire and EMS personnel on the scene. MANHATTAN HIGH-RISE EVACUATED AS OFFICIALS WARN OF POTENTIAL COLLAPSE Democratic New York Gov. Kathy Hochul called the tragedy "absolutely heartbreaking" and pledged the full resources of the state to assist ongoing rescue and investigative efforts. "When people are in their homes feeling that they're secure and safe with their families, to have this horrific incident occur," Hochul said, "it is horrific. New Yorkers deserve to know how and why this happened, and they'll get to the bottom of it, and we'll make sure that we support them in any way." At a press conference on Wednesday evening, Mamdani said the FDNY received a 911 call reporting the collapse at 1321 Flatbush Avenue at 4:01 p.m. Firefighters arrived within one minute and immediately launched efforts to find people who may still be trapped, the mayor said. Rescue crews are deploying drones to survey the wreckage from above and vacuum trucks to safely remove debris as they search for anyone who may still be buried. A cause has not been determined. The city's Department of Buildings (DOB), which has inspectors and engineers on the scene, has launched an investigation. The building, which had a store at street level and apartments upstairs, fell into an open construction site next door at 2625 Bedford Avenue. The developers at 2625 Bedford Avenue had active permits for excavation and foundation work in order to construct a new building, which is set to be three stories tall. In March, the DOB issued a stop work order after inspectors found the developers had demolished the existing building on the site without providing adequate shielding to neighboring properties, including 1321 Flatbush Avenue. Just over a month later, DOB investigators found out that the demolition had continued in violation of the stop work order, which resulted in the contractor being fined $10,000, per city records. By May, the stop work order was lifted after the developers came into compliance, according to the DOB. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The DOB said Wednesday's collapse at 1321 Flatbush Avenue prompted officials to once again halt all work at 2625 Bedford Avenue. Fox News Digital's Eric Mack and Greg Norman-Diamond contributed to this report.

articles.title: 'Not random': Zelenskyy flags 'disruptions' in Musk's Starshield despite Trump's claim
articles.summary: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has again raised concerns over disruptions to Starshield, the military-grade satellite communication service
articles.body: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has again raised concerns over disruptions to Starshield, the military-grade satellite communication service developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX as part of its Starlink technology.He warned that fresh speed restrictions are affecting Kyiv's ability to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and allowing more attacks to get through.In a post on X, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian military units had been facing significant disruptions to Starshield operations for several days across the entire frontline and in temporarily occupied territories.Citing briefings from defence minister Yevhenii Khmara and Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi, he said the service was being subjected to systematic speed restrictions, limiting its operation to 161 kmph.Zelenskyy said Ukrainian military investigations had established that the restrictions were not random technical errors but systematic measures. He warned that the speed cap was complicating efforts to intercept Russian jet-powered drones, with some attacks already getting through because Ukrainian interception systems could not reach the required speeds in time."Unfortunately, this is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine," Zelenskyy said, adding that Kyiv was trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side.The issue was first reported in mid-October, when Ukrainian military units experienced disruptions to Starlink and Starshield connectivity while operating at speeds above 160 kmph. The restrictions affected high-speed drones used for interception missions, long-range strikes and frontline logistics, raising concerns over Ukraine's dependence on SpaceX's satellite communication systems.However, on October 24, Ukraine's defence ministry confirmed that the restrictions had been lifted, with monitoring systems recording stable Starlink and Starshield connectivity at speeds exceeding 400 kmph.Defence minister Yevhenii Khmara said the restoration was crucial for frontline operations, drone missions, logistics and military communications.US President Donald Trump had claimed on October 22 that Elon Musk had restored Ukraine's access to Starshield after reports of restrictions on the satellite communication system.Asked whether he had personally contacted Musk to resolve the issue, Trump declined to confirm, saying, "I don't want to comment on it, you know, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn't make any difference."The latest disruption comes as diplomatic efforts to end the war continue, with US, Ukrainian and Russian delegations concluding two days of trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi on November 11.According to the Associated Press, the negotiations ended with an agreement in principle on a major prisoner exchange, but failed to produce a breakthrough on a broader peace settlement. Territorial disputes and security guarantees for Ukraine remained key sticking points.US President Donald Trump's special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin on the outcome of the negotiations. They are expected to travel to Dublin afterwards to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
